sanskrit: drāvayitvā ca tat sainyaṃ kampayitvā mahārathān nandayām āsa suhṛdo mayaṃ jitveva vāsavaḥ
english: Having routed that army and shaken its great chariot-warriors, he gladdened his friends, as Vāsava once did when he conquered Maya.

sanskrit: tena vidrāvyamāṇāni tava sainyāni saṃyuge cakrur ārtasvaraṃ ghoraṃ parjanyaninadopamam
english: Driven before him in the battle, your forces raised a dreadful cry of anguish, like the roar of a thundercloud.

sanskrit: taṃ śrutvā ninadaṃ ghoraṃ tava sainyasya māriṣa mārutoddhūtavegasya samudrasyeva parvaṇi duryodhanas tadā rājā ārśyaśṛṅgim abhāṣata
english: Hearing that terrible uproar of your army, my lord — like the sea swollen by the wind's force at the time of the full moon — King Duryodhana then spoke to the son of Ṛśyaśṛṅga.

sanskrit: eṣa kārṣṇir maheṣvāso dvitīya iva phalgunaḥ camūṃ drāvayate krodhād vṛtro devacamūm iva
english: This son of Kṛṣṇa's sister, a mighty archer, a second Phalguna as it were, routs our host in his fury, as Vṛtra once routed the army of the gods.

sanskrit: tasya nānyaṃ prapaśyāmi saṃyuge bheṣajaṃ mahat ṛte tvāṃ rākṣasaśreṣṭha sarvavidyāsu pāragam
english: I see no other great remedy for him in this battle save you, O best of rākṣasas, master of all the arts.

sanskrit: sa gatvā tvaritaṃ vīraṃ jahi saubhadram āhave vayaṃ pārthān haniṣyāmo bhīṣmadroṇapuraḥsarāḥ
english: Go swiftly, then, and slay this hero, the son of Subhadrā, in the fray; and we, with Bhīṣma and Droṇa at our head, shall destroy the Pārthas.

sanskrit: sa evam ukto balavān rākṣasendraḥ pratāpavān prayayau samare tūrṇaṃ tava putrasya śāsanāt nardamāno mahānādaṃ prāvṛṣīva balāhakaḥ
english: Thus addressed, that mighty and majestic lord of the rākṣasas advanced swiftly into the fight at your son's command, roaring a great roar like a stormcloud in the rains.

sanskrit: tasya śabdena mahatā pāṇḍavānāṃ mahad balam prācalat sarvato rājan pūryamāṇa ivārṇavaḥ
english: At his mighty cry, O king, the great host of the Pāṇḍavas was set trembling on every side, like the ocean swelling to the full.

sanskrit: bahavaś ca narā rājaṃs tasya nādena bhīṣitāḥ priyān prāṇān parityajya nipetur dharaṇītale
english: And many men, O king, terrified by that roar, gave up their dear lives and fell to the ground.

sanskrit: kārṣṇiś cāpi mudā yuktaḥ pragṛhītaśarāsanaḥ nṛtyann iva rathopasthe tad rakṣaḥ samupādravat
english: And the son of Kṛṣṇa's sister, filled with joy, his bow grasped tight, as though dancing upon his chariot-platform, rushed upon that rākṣasa.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rākṣasaḥ kruddhaḥ saṃprāpyaivārjuniṃ raṇe nātidūre sthitas tasya drāvayām āsa vai camūm
english: Then that enraged rākṣasa, on reaching the son of Arjuna in the battle and taking his stand not far from him, set his host to flight.

sanskrit: sā vadhyamānā samare pāṇḍavānāṃ mahācamūḥ pratyudyayau raṇe rakṣo devasenā yathā balim
english: That great host of the Pāṇḍavas, slaughtered in the battle, advanced against the rākṣasa in the fray, as the army of the gods once marched against Bali.

sanskrit: vimardaḥ sumahān āsīt tasya sainyasya māriṣa rakṣasā ghorarūpeṇa vadhyamānasya saṃyuge
english: A great carnage befell that army, my lord, as it was slaughtered in the battle by the rākṣasa of dreadful form.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarasahasrais tāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahācamūm vyadrāvayad raṇe rakṣo darśayad vai parākramam
english: Then with thousands of shafts the rākṣasa routed that great host of the Pāṇḍavas in the battle, displaying his prowess.

sanskrit: sā vadhyamānā ca tathā pāṇḍavānām anīkinī rakṣasā ghorarūpeṇa pradudrāva raṇe bhayāt
english: And so the army of the Pāṇḍavas, slaughtered by the rākṣasa of dreadful form, fled the battle in fear.

sanskrit: tāṃ pramṛdya tataḥ senāṃ padminīṃ vāraṇo yathā tato 'bhidudrāva raṇe draupadeyān mahābalān
english: Having crushed that army, as an elephant crushes a bed of lotuses, he then rushed in the battle upon the mighty sons of Draupadī.

sanskrit: te tu kruddhā maheṣvāsā draupadeyāḥ prahāriṇaḥ rākṣasaṃ dudruvuḥ sarve grahāḥ pañca yathā ravim
english: But those sons of Draupadī, enraged, mighty archers and fierce strikers, all charged the rākṣasa, as the five planets bear down upon the sun.

sanskrit: vīryavadbhis tatas tais tu pīḍito rākṣasottamaḥ yathā yugakṣaye ghore candramāḥ pañcabhir grahaiḥ
english: Hard-pressed by those valiant warriors, that best of rākṣasas was like the moon beset by five planets at the dread ending of an age.

sanskrit: prativindhyas tato rakṣo bibheda niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ sarvapāraśavais tūrṇam akuṇṭhāgrair mahābalaḥ
english: Then the mighty Prativindhya swiftly pierced the rākṣasa with whetted arrows, all of iron and unblunted at the point.

sanskrit: sa tair bhinnatanutrāṇaḥ śuśubhe rākṣasottamaḥ marīcibhir ivārkasya saṃsyūto jalado mahān
english: His armor cleft by these, that best of rākṣasas shone splendid, like a great cloud shot through with the rays of the sun.

sanskrit: viṣaktaiḥ sa śaraiś cāpi tapanīyaparicchadaiḥ ārśyaśṛṅgir babhau rājan dīptaśṛṅga ivācalaḥ
english: With the gold-shafted arrows clinging to him, the son of Ṛśyaśṛṅga shone, O king, like a mountain with blazing peaks.

sanskrit: tatas te bhrātaraḥ pañca rākṣasendraṃ mahāhave vivyadhur niśitair bāṇais tapanīyavibhūṣitaiḥ
english: Then those five brothers pierced the lord of the rākṣasas in that great fray with whetted arrows adorned with gold.

sanskrit: sa nirbhinnaḥ śarair ghorair bhujagaiḥ kopitair iva alambuso bhṛśaṃ rājan nāgendra iva cukrudhe
english: Pierced by those dreadful arrows, as if by enraged serpents, Alambusa, O king, grew fiercely wrathful, like a king of elephants.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho mahārāja muhūrtam atha māriṣa praviveśa tamo dīrghaṃ pīḍitas tair mahārathaiḥ
english: Sorely pierced, O great king, and hard-pressed by those great chariot-warriors, for a moment, my lord, he sank into a long darkness.

sanskrit: pratilabhya tataḥ saṃjñāṃ krodhena dviguṇīkṛtaḥ ciccheda sāyakais teṣāṃ dhvajāṃś caiva dhanūṃṣi ca
english: Then, regaining his senses and redoubled in his fury, he cut down with his arrows their banners and their bows.

sanskrit: ekaikaṃ ca tribhir bāṇair ājaghāna smayann iva alambuso rathopasthe nṛtyann iva mahārathaḥ
english: And smiling, as it were, Alambusa, that great chariot-warrior, struck each of them with three arrows, as though dancing upon his chariot-platform.

sanskrit: tvaramāṇaś ca saṃkruddho hayāṃs teṣāṃ mahātmanām jaghāna rākṣasaḥ kruddhaḥ sārathīṃś ca mahābalaḥ
english: And in haste and full of wrath, the mighty rākṣasa, enraged, slew the horses of those great-souled warriors and their charioteers as well.

sanskrit: bibheda ca susaṃhṛṣṭaḥ punaś cainān susaṃśitaiḥ śarair bahuvidhākāraiḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: And exulting greatly, he pierced them again with well-whetted arrows of many shapes, by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: virathāṃś ca maheṣvāsān kṛtvā tatra sa rākṣasaḥ abhidudrāva vegena hantukāmo niśācaraḥ
english: Having stripped those mighty archers of their chariots, the rākṣasa, that ranger of the night, rushed upon them with speed, eager to slay.

sanskrit: tān arditān raṇe tena rākṣasena durātmanā dṛṣṭvārjunasutaḥ saṃkhye rākṣasaṃ samupādravat
english: Seeing them tormented in the battle by that evil-souled rākṣasa, the son of Arjuna rushed upon the rākṣasa in the fray.

sanskrit: tayoḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ vṛtravāsavayor iva dadṛśus tāvakāḥ sarve pāṇḍavāś ca mahārathāḥ
english: Between the two there arose a combat like that of Vṛtra and Vāsava; and all your men and all the Pāṇḍava chariot-warriors looked on.

sanskrit: tau sametau mahāyuddhe krodhadīptau parasparam mahābalau mahārāja krodhasaṃraktalocanau parasparam avekṣetāṃ kālānalasamau yudhi
english: Those two, met in the great combat and blazing with wrath against each other, mighty warriors both, O great king, with eyes red with rage, eyed one another in the fight, like the very fire that ends an age.

sanskrit: tayoḥ samāgamo ghoro babhūva kaṭukodayaḥ yathā devāsure yuddhe śakraśambarayor iva
english: Dreadful and bitter in its outcome was the encounter between the two, as in the war of gods and asuras was that of Śakra and Śambara.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca ārjuniṃ samare śūraṃ vinighnantaṃ mahāratham alambusaḥ kathaṃ yuddhe pratyayudhyata saṃjaya
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: How, O Saṃjaya, did Alambusa give battle to the valiant son of Arjuna, that great chariot-warrior, as he was striking down our men in the combat?

sanskrit: ārśyaśṛṅgiṃ kathaṃ cāpi saubhadraḥ paravīrahā tan mamācakṣva tattvena yathā vṛttaṃ sma saṃyuge
english: And how did the son of Subhadrā, slayer of enemy heroes, fight the son of Ṛśyaśṛṅga? Tell me truly all that befell in the battle.

sanskrit: dhanaṃjayaś ca kiṃ cakre mama sainyeṣu saṃjaya bhīmo vā balināṃ śreṣṭho rākṣaso vā ghaṭotkacaḥ
english: And what did Dhanaṃjaya do among my forces, O Saṃjaya, or Bhīma, best of the strong, or the rākṣasa Ghaṭotkaca?

sanskrit: nakulaḥ sahadevo vā sātyakir vā mahārathaḥ etad ācakṣva me sarvaṃ kuśalo hy asi saṃjaya
english: Or Nakula, or Sahadeva, or the great chariot-warrior Sātyaki? Tell me all this, for you are skilled in the telling, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca hanta te 'haṃ pravakṣyāmi saṃgrāmaṃ lomaharṣaṇam yathābhūd rākṣasendrasya saubhadrasya ca māriṣa
english: Saṃjaya said: Come then, I shall recount to you that hair-raising combat, my lord, even as it passed between the lord of rākṣasas and the son of Subhadrā.

sanskrit: arjunaś ca yathā saṃkhye bhīmasenaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca raṇe cakruḥ parākramam
english: And how Arjuna in the fray, and Bhīmasena the Pāṇḍava, and Nakula and Sahadeva, displayed their prowess in the battle.

sanskrit: tathaiva tāvakāḥ sarve bhīṣmadroṇapurogamāḥ adbhutāni vicitrāṇi cakruḥ karmāṇy abhītavat
english: And likewise how all your men, with Bhīṣma and Droṇa at their head, performed wondrous and varied feats without fear.

sanskrit: alambusas tu samare abhimanyuṃ mahāratham vinadya sumahānādaṃ tarjayitvā muhur muhuḥ abhidudrāva vegena tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: Now Alambusa, in the battle, roaring a mighty roar and threatening Abhimanyu, that great chariot-warrior, again and again, rushed upon him with speed and cried out, 'Stand, stand!'

sanskrit: saubhadro 'pi raṇe rājan siṃhavad vinadan muhuḥ ārśyaśṛṅgiṃ maheṣvāsaṃ pitur atyantavairiṇam
english: And the son of Subhadrā too, O king, roaring again and again like a lion in the battle, faced the son of Ṛśyaśṛṅga, that mighty archer, the bitter foe of his father.

sanskrit: tataḥ sameyatuḥ saṃkhye tvaritau nararākṣasau rathābhyāṃ rathināṃ śreṣṭhau yathā vai devadānavau māyāvī rākṣasaśreṣṭho divyāstrajñaś ca phālguniḥ
english: Then the man and the rākṣasa, those two foremost of chariot-warriors, met swiftly in the fray upon their cars, like a god and a dānava — the best of rākṣasas, master of illusion, and the son of Phalguna, knower of celestial weapons.

sanskrit: tataḥ kārṣṇir mahārāja niśitaiḥ sāyakais tribhiḥ ārśyaśṛṅgiṃ raṇe viddhvā punar vivyādha pañcabhiḥ
english: Then the son of Kṛṣṇa's sister, O great king, having pierced the son of Ṛśyaśṛṅga with three whetted shafts in the battle, struck him again with five.

sanskrit: alambuso 'pi saṃkruddhaḥ kārṣṇiṃ navabhir āśugaiḥ hṛdi vivyādha vegena tottrair iva mahādvipam
english: And Alambusa too, full of wrath, swiftly pierced the son of Kṛṣṇa's sister in the breast with nine swift arrows, as one goads a great elephant with hooks.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarasahasreṇa kṣiprakārī niśācaraḥ arjunasya sutaṃ saṃkhye pīḍayām āsa bhārata
english: Then, swift in action, that ranger of the night tormented the son of Arjuna in the combat with a thousand shafts, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: abhimanyus tataḥ kruddho navatiṃ nataparvaṇām cikṣepa niśitān bāṇān rākṣasasya mahorasi
english: Then Abhimanyu, enraged, loosed ninety whetted arrows with smooth-bent joints into the broad chest of the rākṣasa.

sanskrit: te tasya viviśus tūrṇaṃ kāyaṃ nirbhidya marmaṇi sa tair vibhinnasarvāṅgaḥ śuśubhe rākṣasottamaḥ puṣpitaiḥ kiṃśukai rājan saṃstīrṇa iva parvataḥ
english: Swiftly they entered his body, piercing it to the vital parts; and with all his limbs thus pierced, that best of rākṣasas shone, O king, like a mountain strewn with kiṃśuka trees in bloom.

sanskrit: sa dhārayañ śarān hemapuṅkhān api mahābalaḥ vibabhau rākṣasaśreṣṭhaḥ sajvāla iva parvataḥ
english: Bearing those gold-feathered arrows, that mighty best of rākṣasas blazed forth like a mountain wreathed in flame.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho mahārāja ārśyaśṛṅgir mahābalaḥ mahendrapratimaṃ kārṣṇiṃ chādayām āsa patribhiḥ
english: Then, enraged, O great king, the mighty son of Ṛśyaśṛṅga covered the son of Kṛṣṇa's sister, who was the equal of great Indra, with feathered shafts.

sanskrit: tena te viśikhā muktā yamadaṇḍopamāḥ śitāḥ abhimanyuṃ vinirbhidya prāviśan dharaṇītalam
english: The keen arrows loosed by him, like the rod of Yama, pierced clean through Abhimanyu and entered the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: tathaivārjuninirmuktāḥ śarāḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇāḥ alambusaṃ vinirbhidya prāviśanta dharātalam
english: And likewise the gold-adorned arrows loosed by the son of Arjuna pierced clean through Alambusa and entered the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: saubhadras tu raṇe rakṣaḥ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ cakre vimukham āsādya mayaṃ śakra ivāhave
english: But the son of Subhadrā, closing with the rākṣasa in the battle, with smooth-jointed arrows turned him from the fight, as Śakra once turned Maya in combat.

sanskrit: vimukhaṃ ca tato rakṣo vadhyamānaṃ raṇe 'riṇā prāduścakre mahāmāyāṃ tāmasīṃ paratāpanaḥ
english: And the rākṣasa, turned from the fight and slaughtered in the battle by his foe — that scorcher of enemies — then conjured up a great illusion of darkness.

sanskrit: tatas te tamasā sarve hṛtā hy āsan mahītale nābhimanyum apaśyanta naiva svān na parān raṇe
english: Then all upon that field were swallowed up in the darkness; they could see neither Abhimanyu, nor their own, nor the enemy in the battle.

sanskrit: abhimanyuś ca tad dṛṣṭvā ghorarūpaṃ mahat tamaḥ prāduścakre 'stram atyugraṃ bhāskaraṃ kurunandanaḥ
english: And Abhimanyu, beholding that vast and dreadful darkness, that joy of the Kurus brought forth the most terrible weapon of the sun.

sanskrit: tataḥ prakāśam abhavaj jagat sarvaṃ mahīpate tāṃ cāpi jaghnivān māyāṃ rākṣasasya durātmanaḥ
english: Then all the world grew bright, O lord of the earth, and he destroyed that illusion of the evil-souled rākṣasa.

sanskrit: saṃkruddhaś ca mahāvīryo rākṣasendraṃ narottamaḥ chādayām āsa samare śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: And full of wrath, that best of men of mighty valor covered the lord of the rākṣasas in the battle with smooth-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: bahvīs tathānyā māyāś ca prayuktās tena rakṣasā sarvāstravid ameyātmā vārayām āsa phālguniḥ
english: And many other illusions wrought by that rākṣasa the son of Phalguna, knower of all weapons and of measureless spirit, turned aside.

sanskrit: hatamāyaṃ tato rakṣo vadhyamānaṃ ca sāyakaiḥ rathaṃ tatraiva saṃtyajya prādravan mahato bhayāt
english: Then the rākṣasa, his illusions undone and himself smitten with arrows, abandoned his chariot on the very spot and fled in great fear.

sanskrit: tasmin vinirjite tūrṇaṃ kūṭayodhini rākṣase ārjuniḥ samare sainyaṃ tāvakaṃ saṃmamarda ha madāndho vanyanāgendraḥ sapadmāṃ padminīm iva
english: When that rākṣasa, that fighter by trickery, had been swiftly vanquished, the son of Arjuna crushed your army in the battle, as a wild king of elephants, blind with rut, crushes a lotus-pond together with its lotuses.

sanskrit: tataḥ śāṃtanavo bhīṣmaḥ sainyaṃ dṛṣṭvābhividrutam mahatā rathavaṃśena saubhadraṃ paryavārayat
english: Then Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, seeing the army routed, surrounded the son of Subhadrā with a great array of chariots.

sanskrit: koṣṭhakīkṛtya taṃ vīraṃ dhārtarāṣṭrā mahārathāḥ ekaṃ subahavo yuddhe tatakṣuḥ sāyakair dṛḍham
english: Penning in that hero, the great chariot-warriors of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's party, many against one, hewed at him hard with their arrows in the fight.

sanskrit: sa teṣāṃ rathināṃ vīraḥ pitus tulyaparākramaḥ sadṛśo vāsudevasya vikrameṇa balena ca
english: Yet that hero among the chariot-warriors, equal in prowess to his father, was the peer of Vāsudeva in valor and in might.

sanskrit: ubhayoḥ sadṛśaṃ karma sa pitur mātulasya ca raṇe bahuvidhaṃ cakre sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
english: Deeds worthy of both his father and his maternal uncle, in many forms, did he perform in the battle, that best of all who bear arms.

sanskrit: tato dhanaṃjayo rājan vinighnaṃs tava sainikān āsasāda raṇe bhīṣmaṃ putraprepsur amarṣaṇaḥ
english: Then Dhanaṃjaya, O king, striking down your warriors, came upon Bhīṣma in the battle, unable to bear it and longing to reach his son.

sanskrit: tathaiva samare rājan pitā devavratas tava āsasāda raṇe pārthaṃ svarbhānur iva bhāskaram
english: And likewise in the battle, O king, your father Devavrata came upon Pārtha in the fray, as Svarbhānu comes upon the sun.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarathanāgāśvāḥ putrās tava viśāṃ pate parivavrū raṇe bhīṣmaṃ jugupuś ca samantataḥ
english: Then your sons, O lord of peoples, with their chariots, elephants, and horses, surrounded Bhīṣma in the battle and guarded him on every side.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍavā rājan parivārya dhanaṃjayam raṇāya mahate yuktā daṃśitā bharatarṣabha
english: And likewise the Pāṇḍavas, O king, surrounding Dhanaṃjaya, stood armored and arrayed for the great battle, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: śāradvatas tato rājan bhīṣmasya pramukhe sthitam arjunaṃ pañcaviṃśatyā sāyakānāṃ samācinot
english: Then the son of Śaradvat, O king, covered Arjuna, who stood facing Bhīṣma, with five and twenty arrows.

sanskrit: patyudgamyātha vivyādha sātyakis taṃ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ pāṇḍavapriyakāmārthaṃ śārdūla iva kuñjaram
english: Coming up against him, Sātyaki pierced him with keen arrows, for the sake of pleasing the Pāṇḍavas, as a tiger falls upon an elephant.

sanskrit: gautamo 'pi tvarāyukto mādhavaṃ navabhiḥ śaraiḥ hṛdi vivyādha saṃkruddhaḥ kaṅkapatraparicchadaiḥ
english: And the son of Gautama too, in haste and full of wrath, pierced the Mādhava in the breast with nine arrows fledged with heron feathers.

sanskrit: śaineyo 'pi tataḥ kruddho bhṛśaṃ viddho mahārathaḥ gautamāntakaraṃ ghoraṃ samādatta śilīmukham
english: Then the grandson of Śini, that great chariot-warrior, sorely pierced and enraged, took up a dreadful arrow meant to make an end of Gautama's son.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ vegena śakrāśanisamadyutim dvidhā ciccheda saṃkruddho drauṇiḥ paramakopanaḥ
english: As it sped toward him, gleaming like the thunderbolt of Śakra, the son of Droṇa, exceedingly wrathful, cut it in two.

sanskrit: samutsṛjyātha śaineyo gautamaṃ rathināṃ varam abhyadravad raṇe drauṇiṃ rāhuḥ khe śaśinaṃ yathā
english: Then the grandson of Śini, leaving the son of Gautama, that best of chariot-warriors, rushed upon the son of Droṇa in the battle, as Rāhu rushes upon the moon in the sky.

sanskrit: tasya droṇasutaś cāpaṃ dvidhā ciccheda bhārata athainaṃ chinnadhanvānaṃ tāḍayām āsa sāyakaiḥ
english: The son of Droṇa cut his bow in two, O descendant of Bharata, and then, his bow severed, struck him with arrows.

sanskrit: so 'nyat kārmukam ādāya śatrughnaṃ bhārasādhanam drauṇiṃ ṣaṣṭyā mahārāja bāhvor urasi cārpayat
english: Taking up another bow, foe-slaying and equal to its burden, he struck the son of Droṇa, O great king, with sixty shafts upon the arms and breast.

sanskrit: sa viddho vyathitaś caiva muhūrtaṃ kaśmalāyutaḥ niṣasāda rathopasthe dhvajayaṣṭim upāśritaḥ
english: Pierced and shaken, and for a moment overcome with faintness, he sank down upon his chariot-platform, leaning against the staff of his banner.

sanskrit: pratilabhya tataḥ saṃjñāṃ droṇaputraḥ pratāpavān vārṣṇeyaṃ samare kruddho nārācena samardayat
english: Then, regaining his senses, the majestic son of Droṇa, full of wrath, smote the descendant of the Vṛṣṇis in the battle with an iron shaft.

sanskrit: śaineyaṃ sa tu nirbhidya prāviśad dharaṇītalam vasantakāle balavān bilaṃ sarpaśiśur yathā
english: Piercing clean through the grandson of Śini, it entered the surface of the earth, as a young serpent in the springtime enters strongly into its hole.
